caudal_anterior_cingulate.description: The rear part of the anterior cingulate cortex lies on the inner surface of the frontal lobe, above the corpus callosum.
caudal_anterior_cingulate.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with reduced motivation and difficulty adjusting behavior after errors.

caudal_middle_frontal.description: This frontal gyrus lies behind the rostral middle frontal region, near areas involved in preparing movements.
caudal_middle_frontal.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with difficulty holding information in mind and organizing goal-directed actions.

cuneus.description: The cuneus is a wedge of occipital cortex on the inner surface of the hemisphere, above the calcarine sulcus.
cuneus.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with loss of part of the opposite visual field, depending on the affected cortex.

entorhinal.description: The entorhinal cortex lies in the inner temporal lobe and forms a major connection between the hippocampus and other cortex.
entorhinal.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with difficulty forming new memories and finding familiar routes.

fusiform.description: The fusiform gyrus runs along the underside of the temporal and occipital lobes.
fusiform.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with impaired recognition of faces or written words, depending on side and extent.

inferior_parietal.description: The inferior parietal cortex lies below the intraparietal sulcus and combines sensory information with language and spatial processing.
inferior_parietal.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with spatial neglect or difficulty with learned actions and calculation, depending on side.

inferior_temporal.description: The inferior temporal gyrus lies along the lower outer temporal lobe and contributes to identifying complex visual information.
inferior_temporal.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with difficulty recognizing objects despite preserved basic vision.

isthmus_cingulate.description: The isthmus is the narrow posterior part of the cingulate gyrus, linking it with the parahippocampal region.
isthmus_cingulate.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with difficulty using familiar surroundings to orient and recall context.

lateral_occipital.description: The lateral occipital cortex covers the outer back of the hemisphere and processes visual form.
lateral_occipital.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with difficulty recognizing objects from their visual appearance.

lateral_orbitofrontal.description: The lateral orbitofrontal cortex lies on the outer underside of the frontal lobe, above the eye socket.
lateral_orbitofrontal.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with difficulty changing behavior when previously rewarded choices stop being useful.

lingual.description: The lingual gyrus lies on the inner underside of the occipital lobe, below the calcarine sulcus.
lingual.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with visual field changes or difficulty processing written and other complex visual information.

medial_orbitofrontal.description: The medial orbitofrontal cortex lies on the inner underside of the frontal lobe and connects value with decisions.
medial_orbitofrontal.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with altered judgment and difficulty using emotional outcomes to guide choices.

middle_temporal.description: The middle temporal gyrus runs along the outer temporal lobe between the superior and inferior temporal gyri.
middle_temporal.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with difficulty understanding words and accessing knowledge about objects, especially on the language-dominant side.

parahippocampal.description: The parahippocampal cortex lies on the inner underside of the temporal lobe, beside the hippocampus.
parahippocampal.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with difficulty recognizing places and remembering the context of events.

paracentral.description: The paracentral lobule lies on the inner surface of the hemisphere around the upper end of the central sulcus.
paracentral.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with weakness or sensory loss in the opposite leg, depending on the affected portion.

pars_opercularis.description: The pars opercularis is the rear portion of the inferior frontal gyrus, beside the lower precentral cortex.
pars_opercularis.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with effortful speech on the language-dominant side or impaired response control on the other side.

pars_orbitalis.description: The pars orbitalis is the lowest front portion of the inferior frontal gyrus, just above the orbit.
pars_orbitalis.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with difficulty selecting word meanings and retrieving relevant verbal information.

pars_triangularis.description: The pars triangularis is the triangular middle portion of the inferior frontal gyrus.
pars_triangularis.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with difficulty producing fluent language and selecting words, especially on the language-dominant side.

pericalcarine.description: The pericalcarine cortex surrounds the calcarine sulcus on the inner occipital surface and includes primary visual cortex.
pericalcarine.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with loss of vision in the corresponding part of the opposite visual field.

postcentral.description: The postcentral gyrus lies immediately behind the central sulcus and contains primary somatosensory cortex.
postcentral.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with reduced touch discrimination and position sense on the opposite side of the body.

posterior_cingulate.description: The posterior cingulate cortex lies on the inner surface of the hemisphere behind the anterior cingulate region.
posterior_cingulate.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with memory difficulties and problems orienting within familiar surroundings.

precentral.description: The precentral gyrus lies immediately in front of the central sulcus and contains primary motor cortex.
precentral.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with weakness and reduced fine movement on the opposite side of the body.

precuneus.description: The precuneus lies on the inner parietal surface, above the posterior cingulate cortex.
precuneus.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with difficulty in spatial orientation and recalling event details.

rostral_anterior_cingulate.description: The front part of the anterior cingulate cortex curves around the front of the corpus callosum.
rostral_anterior_cingulate.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with changes in emotional regulation and reduced motivation.

rostral_middle_frontal.description: The rostral middle frontal gyrus lies in the front portion of the outer frontal lobe.
rostral_middle_frontal.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with difficulty planning, maintaining goals and switching between tasks.

superior_frontal.description: The superior frontal gyrus runs along the upper frontal lobe beside the midline.
superior_frontal.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with reduced initiative, working-memory problems and difficulty starting movements near its rear portion.

superior_parietal.description: The superior parietal lobule lies in the upper back part of the parietal lobe and combines body and spatial information.
superior_parietal.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with difficulty directing movements toward seen targets and judging body position.

superior_temporal.description: The superior temporal gyrus runs along the upper outer temporal lobe, below the lateral sulcus.
superior_temporal.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with impaired sound processing or speech comprehension, depending on side and extent.

supramarginal.description: The supramarginal gyrus curves around the rear end of the lateral sulcus in the inferior parietal lobe.
supramarginal.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with difficulty repeating speech or performing learned gestures, especially on the language-dominant side.

transverse_temporal.description: The transverse temporal gyri lie within the lateral sulcus on the upper surface of the temporal lobe and include primary auditory cortex.
transverse_temporal.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with impaired sound analysis, with severe hearing loss more likely after damage on both sides.

insula.description: The insula is cortex folded deep inside the lateral sulcus, covered by frontal, parietal and temporal regions.
insula.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with changes in taste, body awareness and emotional processing, depending on the affected portion.

brainstem.description: The brainstem connects the cerebrum and cerebellum with the spinal cord and contains the midbrain, pons and medulla.
brainstem.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with altered alertness, weakness, cranial nerve deficits or disturbed breathing, depending on location.

third_ventricle.description: The third ventricle is a narrow cerebrospinal fluid cavity between the two halves of the diencephalon.
third_ventricle.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with disrupted fluid flow and pressure effects on surrounding tissue when the cavity is obstructed.

fourth_ventricle.description: The fourth ventricle is a cerebrospinal fluid cavity between the brainstem and cerebellum, opening toward spaces around the brain.
fourth_ventricle.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with disrupted fluid circulation and pressure effects when its outlets are obstructed.

optic_chiasm.description: The optic chiasm lies beneath the hypothalamus, where fibers from the nasal half of each retina cross.
optic_chiasm.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with loss of the outer portions of both visual fields when crossing fibers are affected.

lateral_ventricle.description: Each lateral ventricle is a cerebrospinal fluid cavity within a cerebral hemisphere, connected to the third ventricle.
lateral_ventricle.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with disturbed fluid circulation and pressure effects on nearby tissue when outflow is blocked.

inferior_lateral_ventricle.description: The inferior horn of the lateral ventricle extends into the temporal lobe beside the hippocampus.
inferior_lateral_ventricle.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with local fluid trapping and pressure on nearby temporal tissue when its connection is obstructed.

cerebellum_gray_matter.description: Cerebellar gray matter contains neuron cell bodies in the folded cerebellar cortex and deeper nuclei.
cerebellum_gray_matter.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with unsteady movement, inaccurate reaching and impaired balance, depending on the region involved.

cerebellum_white_matter.description: Cerebellar white matter lies beneath the cerebellar cortex and carries fibers between its cortex, nuclei and connections.
cerebellum_white_matter.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with impaired movement coordination and balance from disrupted cerebellar communication.

thalamus.description: The thalamus is a deep collection of nuclei above the brainstem, bordering the third ventricle.
thalamus.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with altered sensation, alertness or memory, depending on the nuclei involved.

caudate.description: The caudate is a curved basal ganglia nucleus that follows the lateral ventricle.
caudate.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with changes in movement, motivation and the ability to organize goal-directed behavior.

putamen.description: The putamen is an outer basal ganglia nucleus beside the globus pallidus and forms part of the striatum.
putamen.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with altered movement speed, control or involuntary movements, depending on the affected circuits.

pallidum.description: The pallidum, or globus pallidus, lies inside the putamen and provides major output from basal ganglia circuits.
pallidum.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with abnormal muscle tone and impaired control of voluntary movement.

hippocampus.description: The hippocampus is a curved structure in the inner temporal lobe, beside the inferior horn of the lateral ventricle.
hippocampus.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with difficulty forming new event memories, especially when both sides are affected.

amygdala.description: The amygdala is a group of nuclei in the front of the inner temporal lobe, near the hippocampus.
amygdala.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with altered recognition of emotional cues and changes in learned responses to threats.

accumbens_area.description: The accumbens area lies in the ventral striatum where the caudate and putamen meet near the basal forebrain.
accumbens_area.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with reduced motivation and altered responses to rewarding outcomes.

ventral_diencephalon.description: This atlas region covers tissue below the thalamus, including hypothalamic and nearby deep structures.
ventral_diencephalon.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with disturbances of sleep, appetite, temperature or hormonal regulation, depending on the tissue involved.

basal_forebrain.description: The basal forebrain lies below the front of the striatum and includes nuclei that send widespread signals to the cortex.
basal_forebrain.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with impaired attention and memory from disrupted signaling to the cortex and hippocampus.

vermal_lobules_i_v.description: Lobules I through V form the upper front portion of the cerebellar vermis along the midline.
vermal_lobules_i_v.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with unsteady posture and difficulty coordinating trunk and leg movements.

vermal_lobules_vi_vii.description: Lobules VI and VII lie in the central upper portion of the cerebellar vermis.
vermal_lobules_vi_vii.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with inaccurate eye movements and impaired balance or trunk coordination.

vermal_lobules_viii_x.description: Lobules VIII through X occupy the lower vermis and include regions linked to balance and vestibular signals.
vermal_lobules_viii_x.whenDamaged: Damage here is associated with unsteady gait, impaired balance and abnormal eye movements.
